anomalies.observed: R1 is a 10M resistor from VCC to the PMOS gate net Net-(Q1-G). That gate is pulled low by Q2, whose base is driven from the PWM net, and JP1 is an open solder jumper, so the default path drives fan power through Q1.
anomalies.expected: A gate pull-up for a PMOS high-side switch that is driven by PWM should be low enough to turn the MOSFET off reliably and quickly, typically on the order of 10k to 100k or smaller with active drive. 10M is orders of magnitude too high for a PWM-driven power switch.
anomalies.impact: The 10M pull-up makes PMOS turn-off very slow and susceptible to leakage/noise. If JP1 is left open and Q1 is used to switch fan power, the fan may remain partially on or PWM speed control via the high-side switch may fail.
